en.title: Hwaljjak Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite (poor appetite), overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion, nausea, and vomiting.
en.usage:
Those aged 15 and over take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Allow at least 4 hours between doses.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children aged 7 or under, patients hypersensitive to soybean oil or with a history of allergic reactions to it, or patients hypersensitive to soybeans or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, or are pregnant or possibly pregnant.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Patients with a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or patients requiring careful administration of lipid emulsions, should take this medicine with caution.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Aipia Soft Capsule
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to relieve dryness of the eyes, for poor development of bone, for the prevention of night blindness and rickets, and to supply vitamins A and D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age.
en.usage:
Adults aged 15 and over take 2 capsules once a day; those aged 7 to under 15 take 1 capsule once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Warning: Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Do not take this medicine if you are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or possibly pregnant.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: if skin itching, nausea, or vomiting occurs after taking, if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, or patients hypersensitive to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or are possibly pregnant.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist when taking together with intravenous lipid preparations.

If diarrhea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Dicamax 1000 Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to supply calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs.
en.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and over take 1 tablet once a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, or patients with hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones, or severe renal failure, or infants under 12 months of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist in the case of children who get plenty of sunlight and eat a normal diet, if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, or have had kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when using together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.title: Baegana Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to improve excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, and indigestion associated with peptic ulcer.
en.usage:
Adults take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day between meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients on dialysis, patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption, women who are pregnant or possibly pregnant, women who are breastfeeding, or children (under 15 years of age).

en.title: Conti 600 Tablet
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and lowered physical strength during or after illness, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness), and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
en.usage:
Children aged 12 and over and adults take 1 tablet once a day after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, infants under 3 months of age, or patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you are deficient in folic acid.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values.

Do not take together with levodopa.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, loose stools, diarrhea, stomatitis (sores in the mouth), loss of appetite, or abdominal bloating, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

다음 분은 복용하지 마세요. 이 약 또는 대두유, 콩, 땅콩에 과민증 환자, 만 12개월 미만의 젖먹이, 심한 증상의 신부전 환자는 이 약을 복용하지 마세요.

en.title: Twice Plus Soft Capsule
en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E and B1 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, and in old age, to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness), for beriberi and eye fatigue, and for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
en.usage:
Adults and those aged 12 and over take 1 capsule at a time, twice a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts, infants under 12 months of age, or patients with severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis, cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, hypoproteinemia, a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, require careful administration of lipid emulsions, are at particular risk from fat overload, or have a predisposition to thrombosis (blood vessel blockage).

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, decreased central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, or if menstruation starts earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier, or bleeding lasts longer, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
